subject: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU capacity MAP for Atlas AI

Subject: Kickoff: Dedicated GPU capacity MAP for Atlas AI

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this forward. We're ready to formalize a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to onboard a dedicated GPU pool for Atlas AI's inference workload. Our goals are to:

- Achieve ~150k tokens/sec sustained for batch inference across our top-3 models.
- Hit p99 generation latency <= 120ms for interactive endpoints.
- Maintain cost predictability for Q2 commitments.

I'd like to kick off a short MAP meeting this week to align stakeholders, confirm throughput targets, and agree on evaluation steps. I've attached a small sample set (atlas_eval_samples.zip) to start the perf evaluation.

Proposed agenda (30 min):
1) Introductions and roles
2) Baseline workloads and metrics
3) Evaluation steps + timeline
4) Pre-procurement checklist / next steps

Who from your side should be the primary technical owner? Also looping in Priya (procurement) on this thread.

Thanks,
Liam

Thanks Naomi — jumping in with a few technical clarifying questions so we can scope the evaluation properly. I'll plan to present these during the kickoff.

Technical questions: 
- Sequence lengths: 1) average 64 tokens, 2) 95th perc 512 tokens, 3) top-3 models vary (decoder-only / chat). Please confirm.
- Batch strategy: do you expect prefixed prompts (static prefix) where we can leverage prefix/KV caching? That affects effective throughput.
- Target latency (p99 120ms) — is that measured from request arrival to final token or per-token?
- Hardware preference: do you have a constraint (A100 80GB, H100, or other)? Some quantization options change throughput by 1.6–2x.
- Estimate of concurrent connections / QPS typical and peak (helps sizing autoscale + reserved capacity).

Suggested pre-MAP evaluation plan (for discussion):
1) Run the sample set through our perf harness on H100 equivalent in our staging pool (2–3 days). 
2) Collect distribution of sequence lengths, token/sec, latency p50/p95/p99, and memory/KV profile.
3) Iterate on batch sizes and quantization to meet the 150k tokens/sec target while hitting p99 SLAs.
4) Draft a proposal: GPU pool size (slots), autoscale policy, and cost estimate.

I'll bring a short perf-run checklist to the meeting and a few example configurations that historically matched similar workloads.

- Sergio

Thanks — quick answers inline:
- Sequence lengths: avg ~72 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens, some rare tails to ~2k.
- 150k tokens/sec: aggregate across our top-3 models (we intend to run them as separate endpoints behind a routing layer).
- Traffic shape: mostly steady batch inference with daily peaks (not pure real-time). We should expect predictable nightly batch windows plus daytime steady load.
- Hardware: we prefer H100 if possible, but open to A100 if the cost delta is significant.
- Concurrent: baseline ~250 concurrent threads, peak ~700.

I've uploaded a sanitized evaluation set to the shared Drive link above and included a short SLO doc in the folder. Priya, who is cc'd, will be our procurement contact.

Let's lock Wed 13th 10:00 PT.

Cheers,
Liam

   - Due: 2026-01-19

2) Commercial / Procurement (owner: Marissa)

   - Deliverable: draft quote + procurement checklist.
   - Due: 2026-01-23

3) Operational handoff (owner: Monica)
   - Prepare runbook for autoscale thresholds, rollback policies, and monitoring dashboards.
   - Deliverable: onboarding runbook + SLO dashboard templates.
   - Due: 2026-02-02

4) Exec review / Close (owner: Naomi)
   - Coordinate internal approvals and schedule executive sync to review commitment + SLA.
   - Target close window: end of February 2026.

Actions requested from Atlas AI:
- Confirm H100 preference vs A100 constraint (Priya) by 2026-01-16.
- Share any additional sample traffic shapes (esp. tails to 2k tokens).
- Confirm procurement contact details for PO routing.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_checklist.pdf (attached), links to Drive and HubSpot above.

If that looks good I will convert this into a shared MAP document and a short Trello/Jira checklist with owner assignments.
